paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches: when trouble comes, the first thing to do is tell God the truth. The people in this prayer don't dress it up. They say, "our rebellions are many; we have sinned against You." Then they ask the hard questions anyway, and they hold on to this: "Yet You are among us, O LORD, and we are called by Your name." (Jeremiah 14:7, 9)

But look at the other voice in this chapter. The prophets keep telling the people, "You will not see the sword or suffer famine, but I will give you lasting peace in this place." The LORD says, "I did not send them or appoint them or speak to them." (Jeremiah 14:13-14) A comfy message is NOT the same as a true one, friend. I've heard plenty of sweet-sounding things in my day, and sweet doesn't mean it came from God.

So why does this matter to you? Because the only way to tell a true word from a pretty one is to know what God has actually said. That's why I bake with the Word every single day, so my ovens stay ready. Come back to it again and again, friend, and you'll know His voice when something else is talking in His name.
